findings.title: Alignment with the 900 container and the plan entry is sound
findings.description: The slice belongs where the plan puts it (entry 26 of `900-slices.maintenance-and-refactoring.md`): it fixes issues #125/#127, is not a new capability, and consumes 925's vocabulary (`CommandTarget`, `DELIVERIES`, `receipt_name`, `write_skill_dirs`) rather than inventing a parallel one. `dependencies: [925]` and the "Interfaces Required" section match what `src/squadron/skills/targets.py` actually exports, and the design's claim that `~/.agents/skills` is the documented Codex user root matches the existing `DELIVERIES[AGENTS].machine_root`. No dependency direction is inverted and no interface is claimed that does not exist.

findings.title: D8 requires doctor to inspect pack sources inside a check layer that is contractually offline and subprocess-free
findings.description: D8 specifies that an agents row for a pack with no Codex content reports `WARN — pack ships no Codex content` rather than "not installed". Deciding that requires reading the pack's *source* root for an `agents/` directory. For `source = "github:..."` packs there is no filesystem path to read: `resolve_source` deliberately raises (`resolver.py:26-27`, "Use clone_github() to resolve github: sources"), and `clone_github` performs a network `git clone` via `subprocess.run`. `doctor_checks.py` states its own contract in its module docstring ("no network, no subprocesses") and the codebase defends that contract elsewhere (`_squadron_skill_names`'s narrow `except (OSError, typer.Exit)`). The design neither says how doctor learns a pack's Codex content nor what the agents row reports when the source cannot be read offline — so criterion 5 is not implementable as written for any pack that is not a local or bundled source, and the verification walkthrough only exercises a local source (`/tmp/p928`). Either pin the offline determination (and the fallback row for an unresolvable source), or cut D8 (see the proportionality finding).

findings.title: The target-scoped receipt filename has no assigned owner on the write path
findings.description: D5 requires the receipt file name to be `base + suffix + scope suffix`, and the slice's value depends on it (`analysis-agents.toml`, criterion 1). But `write_receipt` derives the filename from the payload, not from a key: `target = receipts_dir / f"{receipt.pack_name}.toml"` (`src/squadron/skills/receipts.py:34`). The component change table assigns exactly one change to `skills/receipts.py` — "Gains `remove_receipt_files(receipt) -> int`" — and `State Management` asserts "Schema unchanged; only the file name varies by target and scope (D5)". Nothing in the design says how the writer learns the key: a new parameter on `write_receipt`, a `receipt_key` field on `InstallReceipt`, or `install_pack` passing the suffixed string as `pack_name` (which would also change the stored `pack_name` field). The read side is fine (`read_receipt`'s first argument is already used as the key by `install.py`), so this is the one place D5 does not reach. Name the mechanism and the owning component.

findings.title: Part B's deliverable is deferred to an implementation-time probe, with an open-ended README branch
findings.description: Success criterion 8 requires the shipped rule to carry "the D10 subcommand list", but D10 does not produce that list — it produces a table in which four rows say "confirm by probe", two say "probe", and `sq auth login` is "unprobed", and the design states the rule's contents are "exactly the 'yes' rows" recorded in the implementation DEVLOG. That makes Part B a research task whose output is unknowable at design time, and it leaves one open-ended branch: "If the daemon-client commands need the rule, README's '`$sq-spawn` … fine to invoke directly' sentence is corrected in the same edit" — a docs change to the #126 guidance that is neither scoped nor bounded by a criterion. The probe method itself is a good call (it avoids guessing at Codex's classification), but the design should pin the deliverable: which rows are in the rule under each probe outcome, and whether the README correction is in scope or a follow-up. As written, no reviewer can check the doc half of this slice against the design.

findings.title: Per-target skill-pack doctor rows are new scope beyond the plan entry and are the heaviest machinery in the slice
findings.description: Plan entry 26 assigns Part A as threading `CommandTarget` through `skills install`/`skills uninstall` and Part B as documenting the approval rule; its only doctor question is whether to detect a missing rule, which the design answers "no" (D11). D8 instead adds per-target skill-pack rows, which drags in `installed_path`, the name-format choice, `_command_targets_to_check` reuse, and the unresolved source-resolution problem above — and it is the reason the effort rose from the plan's 2/5 to 3/5. The cuttable scope, in order of value: (1) defer D8's agents rows (and with them the source-resolution gap) to a follow-up, keeping the Claude row byte-identical as the design already promises; (2) drop `--local` from the three `skills` commands — parity with `install-commands` is a nicety, not part of #125, and it costs a root-resolution path plus an ignored-flag warning branch in three commands. `skills list --ide` is defensible (it is one of #125's stated symptoms), and the D4 asset move plus D7 removal extraction are load-bearing for correctness, so those should stay.

findings.title: The collision exclusion understates a new failure mode: a pack can overwrite and then delete squadron's own installed skills
findings.description: The Excluded list calls pack-name collisions "pre-existing on the Claude path and unchanged here". On the Claude path a pack lands in its own `commands_dir/<prefix>/`, so collisions require a shared prefix. On the agents path every pack lands flat in one shared root — the same root 925 writes squadron's bundled skills into — and D3's naming rule permits a pack whose prefix is `analysis` or `sq` to ship `agents/analysis-understand/`. `write_skill_dirs` would copy over squadron's installed `SKILL.md`, the receipt would record that path as the pack's, and `skills uninstall <pack> --ide codex` would then delete a file squadron's own `codex skills` row still counts as installed (the count is name-based, per `_count_installed`). That is issue #65's ownership confusion — the failure the receipt mechanism and `write_skill_dirs`' docstring exist to prevent — arriving through the new target. The design's own D3 rationale leans on "collision reasoning" to justify the name rule, then waves collisions away in Excluded. Either add a collision check against `bundled_skill_names` (and other installed packs) or state explicitly that a name collision silently transfers ownership, so the implementer does not have to rediscover it.

findings.title: Two exhaustive target-keyed tables now describe the same target's layout, with different semantics
findings.description: D6 says "`PACK_LAYOUTS` is the one place that knows where a pack lands", but `DELIVERIES[target]` keeps a `layout` callable, `machine_root`/`local_root`, and `check_subdir`, and `install.py` continues to call `delivery.layout(...)` directly. The two tables disagree for CLAUDE in a way nothing asserts: `write_flat_markdown` writes to `destination / source.name`, while `PACK_LAYOUTS[CLAUDE]` (and `installed_path`) key on `entry.prefix`. That divergence is pre-existing and harmless today only because the bundled subdirectory names coincide with the pack prefixes. Consider extending `TargetDelivery` with the pack-layout fields, or at minimum documenting the split and asserting the two tables agree on the target set and root, so a future target cannot be added to one and forgotten in the other.
